title: Report Generation Flow
summary: Maps the report lifecycle from draft content to final PDF attachment and delivery readiness.
coverage: How findings, checklists, and metadata become report content

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Generated reports are built from data already saved in the database. Unsaved edits in the current browser session are not included in the PDF.

sections.title: Flow objective
paragraphs: RAPTOR supports two report tracks for each pentest record. The generated track builds a structured PDF from report templates and current pentest data. The manual track stores an uploaded PDF file as a record attachment.
Teams typically use generated reports for repeatable operational handoff and governance review, then use manual uploads only when an external document must be attached exactly as provided.

sections.title: Generation prerequisites and gates
paragraphs: Report generation is permission-gated and record-gated. Every request is validated for role capability and assignment access before PDF creation starts.

rows: Request is rejected with `403 Unauthorized access`.
Request is rejected with `403` and assignment-specific message.
Request returns `404 Pentest data not found`.
Template id is valid and enabled
Request returns `400` or `404` depending on failure cause.

sections.title: How report content is assembled
paragraphs: The PDF renderer builds a report model from record metadata, pentest lifecycle fields, vulnerability payload, checklist states, and open ports. It then resolves placeholder tokens and renders template blocks in order.

Checklist coverage is derived from selected checklists plus auto-enabled templates triggered by open ports. Vulnerability severity is derived from CVSS base score and used in both metrics and chart output.

rows: Supports headings, lists, inline code, links, and embedded pentest images.
Common location for analyst narrative and remediation context.
Ports are normalized and mapped to likely service names.
Completion, irrelevant, and unstarted counts are computed per template.
Each finding includes severity, CVSS score, and optional detailed description.

sections.title: Operator sequence in Pentest Record
paragraphs: Use the Overview tab in the pentest record workspace for report operations. The generated report flow is deterministic and should be followed in a fixed order to avoid stale output.
orderedList: Update status, vulnerability flags, dates, notes, checklist states, and findings.
Click `Save Progress` to persist the latest record state.
Choose a template from `Report Template` in `Generated Report`.
Click `Generate Report` and wait for success confirmation.
Validate `Last generated` timestamp and use `Download Generated` for review or distribution.

tip.title: TIP
paragraphs: If the generated report does not reflect your latest edits, save again and regenerate. Generation always reads persisted state, not unsaved editor state.

sections.title: File lifecycle and replacement behavior
paragraphs: Generated and manual report files are stored separately. Regenerating replaces the generated artifact pointer and attempts cleanup of the previous generated file. Manual PDF upload updates the manual `report_file` pointer when the record is saved.
A record can hold both files at the same time. Download actions are separate so teams can compare a template-generated package with an externally authored PDF when required.
